headline: Dry and gradually warmer weather lasts through Saturday around New York, but the odds of rain on Sunday are rising — possibly a soaking Sunday into Sunday night.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tuesday is dry and sunny-to-clear with high pressure centered just west of the area, and temperatures above normal. Winds are light from the northwest early, picking up to around 10 mph by late morning and afternoon and turning to come from the west. Tuesday night stays dry with light winds of 5–10 mph.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday through Friday stay dry as a big dome of high pressure over the middle of the country spreads east. Temperatures stay above normal and creep up slowly day by day; a layer of sinking, warm air aloft acts like a lid, keeping the warm-up gradual. No advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday remains dry and mild. Sunday brings a growing chance of rain as a storm from the Pacific crossing the Mississippi Valley interacts with a second system near the Southeast and Mid-Atlantic coast. If the two combine into a low tracking up the East Coast, Sunday into Sunday night could be a significant rain event; if the system stays farther offshore, much less rain would fall.

coast: High pressure keeps the waters calm through the week with no marine advisories: winds mostly from the northwest to west under 15 knots (about 17 mph) and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 ft.
watch_for: Sunday rain chances are trending up — a coastal storm could bring heavy rain Sunday into Sunday night, or it could slip offshore.
Check back later in the week as forecast models settle on the storm's track and strength.
confidence: High confidence in dry, above-normal-temperature weather through Saturday; low confidence for Sunday, as computer models keep shifting the storm's track and strength from run to run.
